course.title: The Adventures of Pinocchio
course.learnerRule: A learner completes one selected level per session; Foundation, Core, and Studio are alternatives, not cumulative work.

story.guidingQuestionKo: 좋은 습관은 약속만으로 생길까요, 반복으로 생길까요?
story.synopsisKo: 섬에 도착한 피노키오는 일의 가치를 배우고 성장한 요정과 재회해 학교생활을 시작하지만, 아버지 소식에 대한 기대 때문에 다시 약속을 벗어난다.

editorialPolicy.storyFidelity: The twelve sessions preserve the complete original 36-chapter arc, causal sequence, major choices, consequences, reunions, and ending.
editorialPolicy.foundation: Concrete, speakable sentences with one main action and mostly 6–11 words per line.
editorialPolicy.core: Connected sentences with cause, contrast, and reaction, mostly 10–18 words per line.
editorialPolicy.studio: Literary but performable sentences that preserve narrator wit, suspense, and moral tension.
editorialPolicy.safety: Historic peril and slapstick retain their narrative consequence without added graphic detail.
editorialPolicy.narration: Generate one continuous master per session and level; Watch and Mimic must seek within the same performance.
editorialPolicy.classTime: The story text remains concise; sixty minutes comes from deliberate replay, recording, comparison, retrieval, and sentence reconstruction—not padding the narration.

narration.direction: Open with exhausted survival, brighten around honest work and the Fairy reunion, then let school confidence give way to a believable temptation at the beach.
narration.productionRule: Generate one continuous master per session and level; Watch and Mimic seek within that exact same master.

livingStorybook.artBrief: A bright island stage connects the shore and Dolphin, industrious town, water jug and food basket, the grown Fairy's home, classroom, and a path leading toward the shark-watch beach.

lines.text: Pinocchio swam all night and reached an island.
A Dolphin warned him about the Terrible Shark.
The busy islanders would not reward begging.
They offered food only in exchange for work.
At last, Pinocchio carried a woman's water jug.
She gave him bread, vegetables, and sweet candy.
The kind woman was the Blue Fairy.
She had grown while Pinocchio stayed wooden.
Pinocchio promised to study and behave well.
He attended school and ignored early teasing.
Soon he became one of the best students.
The Fairy hoped to make him a real boy.
Some lazy classmates disliked his new habits.
They invited him to see the Shark offshore.
Pinocchio hoped the Shark might reveal Geppetto's fate.
He left school and followed them to the beach.

lines.text: After swimming through the night, Pinocchio reached the Island of Busy Bees.
A helpful Dolphin warned that the Terrible Shark hunted in those waters.
In the busy town, nobody would give food to an able beggar.
Each person offered a meal only if Pinocchio completed honest work.
Hunger finally persuaded him to carry a woman's heavy water jug.
She rewarded him with a generous meal and his favorite candy.
Pinocchio then recognized the woman as the Blue Fairy.
She had grown into a motherly figure while he remained a puppet.
He promised to attend school, work hard, and respect her guidance.
Classmates mocked him at first, but Pinocchio continued studying.
His effort soon made him one of the strongest students.
The Fairy suggested that good habits could eventually make him a real boy.
Several lazy classmates resented the change and planned to distract him.
They claimed that the Terrible Shark had appeared near the beach.
Hoping for news about Geppetto, Pinocchio forgot the school-day promise.
He followed the boys toward the sea and another dangerous test.

lines.text: After battling the sea throughout the night, Pinocchio reached an island whose citizens seemed constantly at work.
A friendly Dolphin warned that the enormous Shark had recently brought terror to the surrounding waters.
Inside the town, every request for food received the same answer: an able person should offer useful labor.
Pinocchio rejected several fair exchanges until hunger finally overcame his old contempt for work.
He carried a woman's heavy jug and basket home, discovering that effort could produce dignity as well as food.
The woman served bread, vegetables, and candy, then watched carefully as recognition reached her guest.
She was the Blue Fairy, now grown into the motherly figure Pinocchio had repeatedly disappointed.
Her growth exposed his own delay: time had moved forward while his habits had kept him wooden.
Pinocchio promised to study, behave responsibly, and earn the possibility of becoming a real boy.
Schoolmates initially mocked the marionette, but he answered ridicule by continuing to learn.
Steady effort made him one of the class's strongest students and began to replace reputation with evidence.
The Fairy encouraged him, explaining that human life required more than simply losing a wooden body.
His laziest companions disliked this transformation and looked for a temptation strong enough to interrupt it.
They announced that the Terrible Shark had appeared offshore and invited him to witness the spectacle.
Concern for Geppetto gave their lie emotional force, because the monster might hold news about his father.
Pinocchio abandoned the school day and followed them to the beach, carrying hope and poor judgment together.
